title: Equal realized derived maps give equal cocycle product classes
statement: Let X be a scheme with the sheaf derived category in its own universe. Let F and G be module sheaves and D,E computing resolution pairings [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data]. Let tD,tE realize their sectionwise pairings [lem-sc-module-cup-resolution-realization]. Assume D.derivedMap(tD)=E.derivedMap(tE), with no degree-zero normalization. In any nonnegative bidegrees p,q, if the two left cocycles have equal class in H^p(X,F), the two right cocycles have equal class in H^q(X,G), and each of the two output cocycles is its respective paired section, then the output classes in H^(p+q)(X,F tensor G) are equal.

source.place: Lemma 20.31.3 and the global cohomology diagram immediately following it

proof.text: For each of D and E apply the naive/derived global cup diagram to the integer extensions of the input complexes. Postcompose with Q(t) and the inverse localized target augmentation. Naturality moves the input augmentation maps across the diagram. The bottom composites agree because the transported derived morphisms agree by hypothesis.

The naive summand formula and Realizes identify the upper diagram values with the specified output cycles. The comparisons to injective resolutions extend the augmentations by over, and computes makes the global homology comparisons invertible. Hence their induced identifications are exactly CupAcyclicResolution.class. Extension by zero identifies the natural and integer degree computations. Take cohomology of the two diagrams and use the equal input classes to obtain equal output classes.

proof_origin.place: Global specialization of Lemma 20.31.3; cocycle equality consequence under equal supplied derived morphisms

theorem moduleCup_equal_derived_maps_class {F G : X.Modules}
    (D E : CupResolutionPairing F G)
    (tD : D.left.integerComplex ⊗ D.right.integerComplex ⟶ D.target.integerComplex)
    (tE : E.left.integerComplex ⊗ E.right.integerComplex ⟶ E.target.integerComplex)
    (hD : D.Realizes tD) (hE : E.Realizes tE)
    (hmaps : D.derivedMap tD = E.derivedMap tE) (p q : ℕ)
    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (ha : D.left.class p a = E.left.class p a')
    (hb : D.right.class q b = E.right.class q b')
    (hc : c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val)
    (hc' : c'.val = E.pair p q ⊤ a'.val b'.val) :
    D.target.class (p + q) c = E.target.class (p + q) c'
